cim: NTT Data: Derry AI centre to create 200 new jobs
cim_eredeti: NTT Data: Derry AI centre to create 200 new jobs
szoveg_eredeti:
One of Japan's largest technology companies is creating around 200 jobs in a new Artificial Intelligence (AI) centre in Londonderry.

NTT DATA announced on Wednesday that it was investing more than £23m to set up a new AI centre of excellence in Derry.

The company, which describes itself as a global leader in AI, digital business and technology services, will recruit 200 people on an average annual salary of £58k to work there over the next three years.

It said it was responding to the worldwide demand in the AI sector.

NTT DATA already has a presence in the north west after acquiring the Derry-based Alchemy Technology Services in October last year.

It is based in Ebrington Plaza and at the time said the 150 staff would work on major transformation projects for insurers worldwide.

The company operates in more than 70 countries providing digital transformation, technology and business services.

The company said this new project would put it in a strong position to respond to the growing demand for AI expertise in financial services, insurance and the public sector.

Invest NI, the economic development agency, has provided more than £2m of funding for the project.

It said it had worked closely with the company's senior worldwide executives to establish the new centre of excellence.

Economy Minister Dr Caoimhe Archibald described the investment as "a huge vote of confidence in the local economy, its people and its future".

"The creation of new jobs, with an average salary of £58,000, will offer exciting career opportunities across AI, data, governance and engineering.

"It is a strong endorsement of our growing reputation as a leading European location for AI and digital innovation and further recognition of the talent and potential we have in the north west."

Charlie Doubek, head of global AI delivery, cloud and security at NTT DATA, said the expansion reflected the strength of the region's talent.

"The region has a significant role to play in delivering our global strategy and this investment reflects our confidence in its ability to support increasingly complex client programmes," he said.

Kieran Donoghue, Invest NI's chief executive, described it as one of their most significant investments in the Derry City and Strabane District Council area in recent years.

"This investment is the product of several visits and engagements with senior NTT executives from Europe, the US, Japan and UK, and illustrates Northern Ireland's capabilities in AI and digital transformation," he said.

The SDLP MP for Foyle, Colum Eastwood, said the investment demonstrated the confidence the company has in the city and its workforce.

"The decision to invest in Derry ahead of other potential locations is a strong endorsement of what our city has to offer," he said.

"This investment in artificial intelligence and emerging technologies gives our city an opportunity to build on its existing strengths in IT services and play a leading role in an industry that will help shape our future economy."
